> **What this document is.** Qualification *evidence*, not a qualification. A
> qualification is a protocol executed and signed by a competent person; no
> script can be that. What this removes is the part a quality reviewer should
> never have to establish by hand — which requirement is implemented by which
> code, checked by which test, and whether that test actually ran and passed.
> Review starts from observed fact rather than from a claim.
>
> Every result below was observed at generation time. A verification that was
> not run reads NOT EXECUTED. A suite that could not start reads ERROR. Neither
> is ever rendered as a pass.

## Intended use

Assembly, publishing and transmission of a submission sequence to an agency.

Surfaces in scope: `submission-center`, `dossier-map`, `ectd-compile`, `ectd-coauthor`, `ectd-publishing`, `gateway-transmittals`

**Reading the impact column.** `direct` means the software itself affects the
integrity, authenticity or content of a regulated record, or decides who may act
on one. `indirect` means it supports that work without producing the record.
The distinction sets the assurance effort: a direct-impact requirement cannot be
discharged by inspection, and the gate refuses a registry that tries.

## Requirement detail

### URS-SUBMISSION-CENTER-02 — The system shall distinguish a read that failed from a read that returned nothing on every Submission Center surface that reports on the record: a failed submission or sequence read renders an explicit error state ("Couldn't load the submissions", and an error rather than "No submission selected" in the per-sequence workspaces), a failed compilation-history read is never rendered as "No compilations yet", and the eCTD Co-Author backbone footer withholds its document, approved and readiness figures unless documents were actually read.

**Intended use.** A regulatory director checks whether a submission exists, whether a sequence was ever compiled, and how complete an eCTD backbone is. Each of those readings is a statement about the regulated record, and an outage must be reported as an outage rather than as an answer of "none" or "0%".

**If it fails.** A 401/500/malformed response collapses to an empty array and the surface renders "No submissions yet", "No compilations yet" or a computed "0% eCTD readiness"; the user concludes that a filing, a compilation history or an assembled dossier does not exist when the system simply could not read it, and proceeds (or reports to an agency) on that basis.

**CSA impact.** indirect · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-SUBMISSION-CENTER-03 — The system shall refuse a request to move an eCTD sequence to `frozen` or `dispatched` through the ordinary lifecycle-transition endpoint with GOVERNED_REQUIRED, and shall produce either state only through the governed applier, which requires an executed Part 11 `sign` action recorded on the exact `ectd-sequence:<id>` target by the same actor and declaring that step's own intent.

**Intended use.** Freezing and dispatching are the irreversible, outward-facing acts of a filing. A regulatory operations lead performs them from the Dispatch workspace only through the Part 11 e-signature dialog, and the platform must be able to show an inspector the signature that authorized each one.

**If it fails.** A caller (or the UI) posts status='frozen' to the generic transition endpoint and the sequence becomes frozen or dispatched with no electronic signature; the submission record then carries an irreversible state change with no attributable human authorization, which a Part 11 inspection would read as an unsigned approval of a regulatory submission.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high

### URS-SUBMISSION-CENTER-04 — The system shall refuse a governed freeze, dispatch or transmit whose signature declares a different step's intent, has already authorized a governed transition, has been revoked, is not bound to the sequence's leaf manifest, or whose bound digest no longer equals the current leaf-manifest digest — requiring the sequence to be signed again for its current content.

**Intended use.** Each irreversible step of a filing carries its own meaning under 21 CFR Part 11 §11.50, and §11.70 requires the signature to be linked to the content it signed. A publisher who edits a leaf after signing must re-sign before the sequence can be frozen or sent.

**If it fails.** One signature is replayed to freeze, dispatch and transmit, or a leaf is swapped after signing and the altered dossier is frozen under a signature applied to different bytes; the platform would then attest that a named human approved content they never saw, and the signature manifest in the record would be false.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high

### URS-SUBMISSION-CENTER-05 — The system shall compute the dispatch gate's inputs server-side from the sequence's own leaves and its open critical Shadow Review findings (never from client-supplied counts), refuse a freeze or dispatch with DISPATCH_BLOCKED while the gate for that step is not cleared, and render the server's blockers verbatim in the Dispatch workspace — offering no freeze or dispatch control while the gate blocks or while the readiness read fails, and offering the Part 11 e-signature-gated control only when the gate is clear and the sequence holds the required state.

**Intended use.** Before a sequence is frozen or dispatched, a submission manager reads the gate to see exactly what still blocks the filing — structural validation errors, unacknowledged critical shadow-review findings, a missing release signature — and the gate, not the user, decides whether the act may proceed.

**If it fails.** A client passes validationErrors: 0, or the surface offers the freeze button while the server gate blocks, and a sequence with unresolved structural errors or open critical findings is frozen and dispatched — a defective dossier reaches the agency and the platform's own record shows it as cleared.

### URS-SUBMISSION-CENTER-06 — The system shall refuse to create, update or delete a submission leaf on a frozen or dispatched sequence, and shall refuse at the write boundary any leaf whose section code is not a well-formed CTD section code (a bare module number, a module outside 1-5 or an unparseable value is refused; the code is not checked against the published ICH/FDA heading tables), whose document table is not a placeable document store, or whose key space (integer document_id versus uuid document_uuid) does not match that store.

**Intended use.** The Builder workspace is where a document is placed into a CTD section of a sequence. The placement decides where the document appears in the assembled package, so an unresolvable or misfiled pointer is a defect in the submission's content, and a frozen sequence's contents must not change.

**If it fails.** A mistyped section code becomes a literal folder name in the package, or a misspelled document table is stored, audited as a placement and reported dispatch-clear, and the leaf only fails to resolve at assembly — at the end of a filing window; or a leaf is edited after freeze, so the frozen dossier is not the one that was signed.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-SUBMISSION-CENTER-08 — The system shall require, for every agency-gateway transmit and every rollback, a reason of at least eight characters and a server-verified §11 re-authentication, record the governed action and electronic signature with only the authentication factors actually verified, and surface the server's refusals — 401 re-auth failed, 409 an active transmittal holds the lock, 412 gateway credentials not configured, 422 structural gate with its findings — in the server's own words without claiming anything was sent.

**Intended use.** Gateway Transmittals is the last screen before bytes leave for FDA ESG, EMA CESP, PMDA and the other regional gateways. The operator re-authenticates and states a reason, and every refusal has to be legible so they know whether the submission left the platform.

**If it fails.** A transmit runs without verified re-authentication or without a recorded reason, or a refusal is rendered as a generic failure; the platform then holds no attributable authorization for a filing that reached an agency, or an operator re-sends a package that is already in flight because the 409 lock was reported as an ordinary error.

### URS-SUBMISSION-CENTER-09 — The system shall state the provenance of every downloaded transmittal acknowledgement in the document's heading, its filename and the X-Ack-Provenance response header — agency bytes only where the gateway returned them (the FDA AS2 MDN), and otherwise this platform's own record of what it sent — and the surface shall tell the user which of the two arrived.

**Intended use.** A sponsor archives a gateway acknowledgement as evidence that an agency received a submission on a given date. The archived file must be self-describing, because it will be read long after the screen that served it is gone.

**If it fails.** A text file composed by the platform from its own transmittal row is downloaded as "ack-<id>.txt" and archived as agency correspondence; in a filing-date dispute or an inspection the sponsor is shown to have represented a self-authored document as an agency receipt, and holds no agency receipt at all.

### URS-SUBMISSION-CENTER-10 — The system shall refuse a sequence transmit that names no target environment or no agency application number rather than defaulting to production or writing an invented identifier into the backbone, and shall block the transmit with DISPATCH_BLOCKED, naming every leaf, when any leaf's source cannot be materialized into the package; where the organization holds no gateway credentials for the chosen environment it shall report transmitted:false with reason gateway_not_configured rather than reporting a send.

**Intended use.** Transmit is the one irreversible act in the platform. The operator chooses staging or production explicitly, and the package that goes must physically contain every document the backbone references.

**If it fails.** An omitted environment defaults to production and a test package is filed to the live agency endpoint; or a sequence transmits with an "UNASSIGNED-SEQ-<id>" application number in the regional backbone; or a leaf whose bytes live in external storage is silently dropped from the ZIP and the agency receives a dossier missing a document its own index.xml lists.

### URS-SUBMISSION-CENTER-11 — The system shall compile through the real package generator only where the programme resolves to a canonical submission spine with placed leaves, and shall otherwise emit a draft backbone whose every leaf carries rendered="false" with no file path and no checksum, reporting submissionReady only when submissionBlockers is empty and otherwise stating, from the spine's actual state, exactly why no leaf file exists.

**Intended use.** The eCTD Compile surface tells a publisher whether the programme can produce a submittable package and hands them the backbone XML it produced. The artifact and the verdict are what the publisher acts on.

**If it fails.** The draft backbone declares <ectd:file-path> entries for files that were never written and checksums that were never computed, and the response says "Submission-ready" beside a download button; a publisher downloads and forwards a backbone that references non-existent leaf files as if it were an assembled package.

### URS-SUBMISSION-CENTER-12 — The system shall render the eCTD qualification spec versions and the controlled-vocabulary lists on the Publishing Center only from a response that matches the declared shape — routing a malformed or wrong-shaped 200 to the error state rather than to an empty one, and distinguishing the pre-read idle frame from an empty result — and shall offer no freeze, dispatch, transmit or publish action from that surface.

**Intended use.** A publisher checks which exact ICH/FDA eCTD specification versions a package is qualified against and which controlled-vocabulary codes and OIDs apply, before building a v3.2.2 or v4.0 submission. It is a reference and validation view only.

**If it fails.** A proxy or version skew returns a plausible but wrong body and the panel renders "No spec versions" or "No codes"; the publisher concludes the package is qualified against nothing, or that a controlled vocabulary has no codes, and selects an attribute value the agency's validator will reject.

### URS-SUBMISSIONCENTER-90 — The system shall return a visitor with no session from the Submission Center surface `submission-center` to sign-in, and shall render that surface only once a session is established.

**Intended use.** A regulatory user reaches Submission Center through an authenticated session. The record this surface exposes is a regulated one, so an unauthenticated visitor must be returned to sign-in rather than shown any part of it.

**If it fails.** The surface renders for a visitor with no session, exposing a regulated record to an unidentified person and breaking the attribution every audit entry depends on.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high
